blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-performance-1 (One customer query per invoice in the monthly report) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: N+1 queries: `customer_label` is called once per invoice inside the loop of `monthly_report` (src/report.rs:23-26), so a month of about 3 000 invoices runs about 3 000 `SELECT ... FROM customers WHERE id = $1` queries, growing linearly with the month's invoices, while only about 800 distinct customers exist. `Db::customers(&[i64])` (src/db.rs:26, `WHERE id = ANY($1)`) already serves the whole set: collect the distinct `customer_id`s, load them in one call, index them in a `HashMap<i64, Customer>` and build each label from it, keeping the invoice-number order and returning the same error when a customer is missing.
findings.title: One customer query per invoice in the monthly report

findings.recommendation: `purchase_order` is called for every invoice (src/report.rs:28) and compiles the regex on each call, so a 3 000-invoice month compiles the same pattern 3 000 times — compiling a pattern is expensive compared with matching one short note. Compile it once, in a `static` `std::sync::LazyLock<Regex>` (or `once_cell`), and reuse it; the matches stay the same.
findings.title: The purchase-order pattern is compiled once per invoice
